description: Coral's Gemma RVV kernels as self-checking guest programs. Each program generates deterministic inputs, calls the unmodified upstream kernel, compares the result with a reference and prints a pass marker.

conventions.isa: RV32 with RVV, VLEN=128. FP32 math uses e32m8 vectors; BF16 data is widened to FP32 on load (vfwcvtbf16) and narrowed on store (vfncvtbf16).
conventions.bf16: BF16 is stored as raw 16-bit values (upper half of an IEEE binary32, round to nearest even).
conventions.layout: Row-major. The kernel_* programs keep their buffers in DTCM (512 KiB layout); the rvv_matmul_* programs use external RAM at 0x20000000. Every program leaves guard words after the output and fails if any change.
conventions.cycles: Harnesses report the sum of mcycle deltas around the kernel calls. Cycle counts are meaningful on the RTL simulators only; MPACT has no timing model.
conventions.pass_marker: Each program prints <marker>_CASE lines, then <marker>_PASS cases=N cycles=C max_abs_error_e9=E, or <marker>_FAIL with the failing index. E is the largest absolute error times 1e9.

kernels.summary: Elementwise residual addition of two tensors.
kernels.operation: Y[i] = A[i] + B[i] for i in [0, total_elements)

variants.signature: void rvv_residual_add_f32(const float* A, const float* B, float* Y, size_t total_elements)
void rvv_residual_add_bf16(const __bf16* A, const __bf16* B, __bf16* Y, size_t total_elements)

shapes_checked: 1x33 (rows x hidden; the kernel sees rows*hidden elements)
kernels.reference: A + B in FP32 from the (BF16-rounded) inputs

kernels.summary: Gemma RMS normalisation of each row, scaled by (1 + weight).
kernels.operation: for each row x of hidden_size elements: y[j] = x[j] * rsqrt(mean(x^2) + epsilon) * (1 + weight[j])

variants.signature: void RmsNormF(size_t seq_len, size_t hidden_size, float epsilon, const float* input, const float* weight, float* output)
void RmsNormBf16(size_t seq_len, size_t hidden_size, float epsilon, const __bf16* input, const __bf16* weight, __bf16* output)

kernels.reference: double-precision sum of squares, then FP32 x * (1/sqrt(mean + epsilon)) * (1 + weight)

kernels.summary: Gated activation used in Gemma MLP blocks: tanh-approximated GELU of the gate, multiplied by the up projection.
kernels.operation: out[i] = 0.5 * g * (1 + tanh(sqrt(2/pi) * (g + 0.044715 * g^3))) * up[i], with g = gate[i]

variants.signature: void rvv_tanh_gelu_mul_f32(const float* gate, const float* up, float* output, size_t total_elements)
void rvv_tanh_gelu_mul_bf16(const __bf16* gate, const __bf16* up, __bf16* output, size_t total_elements)

shapes_checked: 1x33 (rows x hidden; the kernel sees rows*hidden elements)
kernels.reference: the formula above in FP32 with libm tanhf
kernels.notes: The kernel evaluates tanh with a rational approximation clamped to [-3, 3]; the tolerance covers that.

kernels.summary: FP32 matrix multiply: a GeMV for one row, a tiled kernel for more.
kernels.operation: C[m][n] = sum over k of A[m][k] * B[k][n]; A is MxK, B is KxN, C is MxN, all row-major

variants.signature: void rvv_gemv_1d_f32(const float* A, const float* B, float* C, int K, int N); void rvv_tiled_matmul_2d_f32(const float* A, const float* B, float* C, int M, int K, int N)

kernels.reference: integer-valued operands, so the products and sums are exact; compared bit for bit
kernels.notes: Weights live in external RAM at 0x20000000; this program uses the 1 MiB TCM layout. See examples/README.md.

kernels.summary: INT8 matrix multiply with INT32 accumulation.
kernels.operation: C[m][n] = sum over k of int32(A[m][k]) * int32(B[k][n]); A is MxK int8, B is KxN int8, C is MxN int32

variants.signature: void rvv_gemv_int8(const int8_t* A, const int8_t* B, int32_t* C, size_t K, size_t N); void rvv_matmul_int8(const int8_t* A, const int8_t* B, int32_t* C, size_t M, size_t K, size_t N)

kernels.notes: Either A or B must be quantised symmetrically (-128 on at most one side), otherwise the widening accumulation can overflow.

kernels.summary: BF16 matrix multiply with BF16 output.
kernels.operation: C[m][n] = bf16(sum over k of A[m][k] * B[k][n]); A is MxK, B is KxN, C is MxN, all BF16 row-major

variants.signature: void rvv_gemv_1d_bf16(const __bf16* A, const __bf16* B, __bf16* C, int K, int N); void rvv_tiled_matmul_2d_bf16(const __bf16* A, const __bf16* B, __bf16* C, int M, int K, int N)

kernels.reference: integer-valued operands; the exact sum rounded to BF16 (round to nearest even) must match bit for bit
